title: Classes and objects in Java
answer: A class is a type definition or blueprint that declares the state and behavior shared by its instances. An object is a runtime instance of that class with its own identity and field values. In AeroTopo, `Orthomosaic` is a class defining fields, construction rules, and behavior inherited from `Product`; each `new Orthomosaic(...)` creates a distinct object whose id, tiles, and resolution values belong to that instance. Static members belong to the class itself, while instance members belong to individual objects.
